rationale:
Evidence: all 60 trials of every design so far ended off track at max_error of about 0.06 m, the off-track limit for any allowed body width. RMS error sits near 0.03 m everywhere. Iteration 5 (score 137.76) is the best design so far: body 0.14 x 0.10 m, 0.5 kg, five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.06 to +0.06 and y = 0.07, wheel_track 0.12, kp 3.0, kd 0.4, ki 0, base_speed 1.3, last_direction line loss.

Several single-parameter changes produced metrics identical to four decimals, so those levers are not binding: kd 0.4 vs 1.0, ki 0 vs 1.0, wheel_track 0.12 vs 0.10, base_speed 1.3 vs 1.1, and the wider sensor span to +/-0.08 at y = 0.08. Iteration 10 (kp 5.0) lowered the score to 105.5 and did not change the s-bend result, so raising kp is not the answer either. The s-bend result (77.71) is identical across kp 3 and kp 5, which suggests the failure happens at a point the controller barely affects. I do not have a tested change that addresses it.

Change: none in substance. I am delivering the iteration-5 design with wheel_track set to 0.10 m. Iterations 7 through 9 show that this value gives identical metrics, and it is the value on the current scoreboard, so the design is a known, reproducible baseline. Untested changes at the final iteration carry risk that the unseen-track race cannot recover from, and no tested change has beaten 137.76.

Expected result: about 137.8 on the development tracks, with progress near 0.55 on the oval and off-track ends elsewhere. The unseen track may differ, so this is a robustness-first choice rather than an expected improvement.
